chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever causes harm with something from the roads of the Muslims, he is responsible for it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on liability for harm caused in public roads?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith articulates the principle of 'daman' (financial liability) for harm caused by public infrastructure, specifically linking it to the chapter on those who dig wells. It underscores the juristic consensus that the owner or digger bears responsibility for injuries sustained by passersby, reflecting the broader Shia legal emphasis on public safety and compensation. This ruling serves as a foundational precedent for modern applications of tort law within Islamic jurisprudence.
